key_insight: Tango introduces a hybrid token-pruning strategy that explicitly accounts for multi-modal, long-tailed attention distributions and preserves rare but important visual signals, enabling much more efficient Video LLMs without sacrificing comprehension.
problem_solved: Existing token-pruning methods (top-k attention selection and similarity-based clustering) either neglect complex attention shapes or discard low-magnitude yet semantically important tokens, causing information loss and suboptimal efficiency-accuracy trade-offs in video-language models.
method: Attention-distribution-aware selection: replace naive top-k with adaptive thresholds and multi-modal peak detection so selection follows spatially multi-modal, long-tailed attention patterns.
Signal-preserving clustering: improve similarity-based merging by weighting clusters with attention-derived importance and preserving rare/high-value tokens via residual encoding.
Hybrid scheduler (Tango): combine the above into a lightweight, runtime-aware pruning pipeline that adaptively balances token sparsity and fidelity across frames.
impact: Practitioners can deploy Video LLMs that run faster and use less compute while maintaining understanding of temporally and spatially subtle visual cues—useful for real-time video analysis, multimodal agents, and resource-constrained deployments.

paper_title: Tango: Taming Visual Signals for Efficient Video Large Language Models
paper_authors: Shukang Yin, Sirui Zhao, Hanchao Wang, Baozhi Jia, Xianquan Wang
